records.quote: Fundamentally, the unique buoyancy-free environment offered by microgravity affords simple aerodynamic flow fields to acquire diffusion flame data of high fidelity, with the prospect of understanding unit thermochemical processes as well as quantifying the associated physico-chemical parameters.
records.derivation: Rationale for the investigation, not a statement that these tests were run in microgravity. section=projectType is only the PSI category label 'Microgravity Investigation'. The direct statements are in the final report (R2, R3).

records.quote: The project has completed two (2) rounds of microgravity experimentation.
records.derivation: Section 4.C 'Summary of Preliminary Results'. Covers both rounds (test days 19254 to 20190). The report adds that the acceleration environment was not evaluated, page=42: 'It is possible that the tests are subtly affected by the acceleration environment, but there is not obvious indication of this and it has thus far not been evaluated with available measurements from the Space Acceleration Measurement System (SAMS).'

records.quote: The basic flame configuration adopted for the investigation is the spherically symmetric diffusion flame generated by discharging a fuel gas from a porous spherical burner into a quiescent, oxidizing atmosphere in microgravity.
records.derivation: Same section 4.C. A near-identical sentence copied from the 2010 SRD is on page=3 (with the typo 'fuel gasfrom').

records.quote: Conventional gaseous fuels including hydrogen, methane, and ethylene will be used.
records.derivation: PSI record text, written as a plan ('will be used'). section=subResearchArea also reads 'Flames of gaseous fuels'.

records.quote: Conventional gaseous fuels including hydrogen, methane, and ethylene are used.
records.derivation: Section 4.C of the final report, written after both test rounds.

records.quote: International Space Station (ISS)
Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME
records.derivation: The ACME chamber insert in the CIR is shared with the other ACME investigations named in the report (CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, BRE, Flame Design, CFI-G). See lineage.

records.quote: The Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (s-Flame) experiment is one of six independent experiments that make up the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) project for which tests are conducted within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the International Space Station (ISS).
records.derivation: Section 1 'Overview'. The CIR named in the same sentence is proposed in R9.

records.quote: The s-Flame experiment uses the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) and the ACME hardware in the Destiny module of the ISS.
records.derivation: Section 4.C. 'ACME hardware' is the ACME chamber insert shared by the ACME investigations. See lineage.

records.quote: *Atmosphere is ~1 atm but pressure increases and O2% drops with vitiation.
records.derivation: Notes column, data row 2: the footnote for the Atmosphere column, applying to all test days. Approximate nominal chamber pressure; the same note says pressure increases with vitiation but gives no value for the increase.

records.quote: Atmosphere is ~1 atm but pressure increases and O2% drops with vitiation.
records.derivation: Footnote 2 under Table 1 'Flames ignited for the s-Flame experiment' (preceded by a superscript '2' in the PDF). The same footnote is under the Appendix D table on page=60. Context, page=17: 'All ACME experiments will be constant volume (i.e., rather than constant pressure) studies, where the chamber’s free volume will be about 90 liters.'

records.quote: These tests were conducted with a mixture of hydrogen (20%), methane (25%), and nitrogen (55%) ejected from the porous spherical burner into a chamber atmosphere of air (21% oxygen, 79% nitrogen at 1 atm).
records.derivation: Appendix G (Payload Weekly Science Summary), 'Week 15: January 3 - 9', describing GMT 006, i.e. test day 20006. Agrees with the ~1 atm note (R10, R11).

records.quote: The fuel and nitrogen both flow from the burner sphere into a chamber atmosphere of ~19% oxygen and nitrogen at a pressure of ~1 atm.
records.derivation: Appendix G, 'Week 16: January 10 - 16', caption of a figure showing four tests from GMT 013 (test day 20013). The oxygen value in the same sentence is proposed in R14.

records.quote: The fuel and nitrogen both flow from the burner sphere into a chamber atmosphere of ~19% oxygen and nitrogen at a pressure of ~1 atm.
records.derivation: Disagrees with the PSI table: CSV row=7 (test day 20013) Atmosphere reads '~21% O2 with N4'. Inside the same report, Table 1 (page=24) gives '~21% O2, with N2' for this day and page=27 says 'Test day 20013 mainly investigates 30% H2 /15% CH4 / 55% N2 mixtures issuing into air.' This page-79 sentence comes from the weekly operations summary and describes four specific tests. The table note (CSV row=2) says 'O2% drops with vitiation'; the report does not say whether that explains ~19%. Both values kept, not resolved. Percent basis: the report states it elsewhere as volume (page=19: 'an oxygen concentration of nominally 21% (on a volume basis)').

records.quote: Although 13 tests were conducted with the 21% O2/He atmosphere, ignition was not achieved.
records.derivation: PSI table CSV row=15 (test day 20164) Atmosphere reads only '~30% O2 with He'. The report says tests at 21% O2/He were also run that day, all without ignition; page=68: 'The 20164 tests began study of ethylene-based flames, where 20% C2H4/80% He issued into 30% O2/He and 21% O2/He atmospheres.' The table counts flames ignited; neither source says whether its Atmosphere column is meant to cover non-ignited tests. Percent basis: see R14.

records.quote: A last set of tests were conducted with a reduced oxygen concentration atmosphere, i.e., 17.5% O2/82.5% He.
records.derivation: PSI table CSV row=18 (test day 20190) Atmosphere reads '~30% and ~21% O2 with He'; the report adds a last set of tests at 17.5% O2 on that day. Also stated on page=29: 'Tests with a reduced oxygen concentration atmosphere of 17.5% O2 / 82.5% He seems to show both radiative and kinetic extinction.' The diluent (He) agrees with the table. Percent basis: see R14.

records.quote: Test day 19256 uses nitrogen-diluted C2H4 issuing into 21% O2 / 79% N2 atmosphere to examine kinetic extinction at low system Damköhler numbers.
records.derivation: PSI table CSV row=2 (test day 19256) Atmosphere reads '~21% O2 with N3' (and Fuel Bottle '50% C2H4 with N3'); 'N3' is not a diluent gas. The report's Table 1 (page=24) gives '~21% O2 with N2' for this day. Oxygen (~21%) agrees. The '2' digits are subscripts in the PDF.

records.quote: Test day 19304 investigates 45% CH4 / 55% N2 mixtures issuing into 21% O2 / 79% N2 atmosphere.
records.derivation: PSI table CSV row=3 (test day 19304) Atmosphere reads '~21% O2 with N4'; 'N4' is not a diluent gas. The report's Table 1 (page=24) gives '~21% O2 with N2' for this day. Oxygen (~21%) agrees.

records.quote: ~21% O2, with N2
records.derivation: Table 1, Atmosphere column: this cell is merged over test days 19352, 20006, 20013, 20024 and 20029. The PSI table reads differently for four of them: CSV row=6 (20006) '~21% O2 with N3', row=7 (20013) '~21% O2 with N4', row=8 (20024) '~21% O2 with N5', row=9 (20029) '~21% O2 with N6'; N3 to N6 are not diluent gases. Row=5 (19352) reads N2 and agrees, so 19352 is not listed here. The Appendix C table (page=49) has the same cell text. For 20006 and 20013, page=27 also says the mixtures issued 'into air'.

records.quote: The 20132 tests kicked off a round of tests with helium-diluted fuel and oxidizer. The ambient was 21% O2 and 79% He.
records.derivation: PSI table CSV row=10 (test day 20132): the Atmosphere column reads '~21% O2 with He' and agrees, but the Test Type column of the same row reads 'First round of tests with nitrogen-diluted fuel and oxygen'. The report puts 20132 under 'Second round of tests, with helium-diluted fuel and oxygen' (Table 1, page=24), and page=18 calls it 'the first test day with helium (11 May 2020, i.e., 20132)'.

not_found.looked_in: PSI record text (all sections); CSV Notes rows 1-3; final report pages 1-114. No normal-gravity tests are reported as part of this investigation's ISS test set. Pages 4-5 (copied from the 2010 SRD) describe earlier drop-tower, parabolic-aircraft and normal-gravity work only as background ('Previous experimentation on earth has amply demonstrated this influence.'); page 84 mentions 'preliminary ground-based testing' with no test ids or conditions. No normal_gravity record proposed.

PSI record text (section=approach says pressures are measured, no value); CSV Notes row=2; final report pages 1-114. No numeric value for the pressure rise: page 21 says only 'The pressure rise with an s-Flame test was small', and page 17 says burner flows 'will generally be constrained to limit the pressure rise'. Only the nominal ~1 atm is proposed (R10-R13).

lineage: s-Flame ran on the ACME chamber insert in the CIR on the ISS, shared with the other ACME investigations named in the report (CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, BRE, Flame Design, CFI-G). Final report page=9: 'As previously discussed, the ACME experiments will be conducted within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) using a chamber insert, depicted in Figure 2, which was designed to accommodate gas delivery to a variety of exchangeable burners.' It also used the same burner as Flame Design (page=20: 'Similarly, the s-Flame experiment was conducted using the same burner as the Flame Design investigation which preceded it.'). Sections 3.A and 4.B of the report are copied from ACME-wide documents (ACME Engineering Implementation; a 2014 conference paper; a 2018 E-FIELD Flames paper), so their hardware text is shared across ACME reports. The report says 'one of six' ACME experiments (page=3); the ISS daily summaries it quotes say 'one of five' (pages 92-96). E-FIELD Flames uses an electric field; it is not a gravity data point.
